report.summary: Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A quoted 335 on both bid and ask, re-quoting every 1-4 s. Each bid/ask pair was cancelled together and replaced. The detector's 'BUY cancelled after SELL execution' triggers are fills on the trader's own ask quote, with the paired bid pulled at the same moment as part of the re-quote. No single order approached the depth (max 0.13x), and quote size matches the desk norm. There is no one-sided resting order, so features (a) and (b) are both absent. Close as a false positive on market making.

response.final_text:
**Proposed disposition:** CLOSE_FP, confidence 0.85. The case is on file and awaits a human decision.

**What drove it:**
1. T-MM-02 is a registered market maker on SYN.A. It quoted 335 on both bid and ask and re-quoted every few seconds. Cancel symmetry is 0.986, and the largest resting order was 0.13× depth, so there is no large one-sided order.
2. The detector's "BUY cancelled after a SELL fill" triggers are fills on the trader's own ask quote (211, 156 and 89). The paired bid was pulled in the same re-quote, so there is no resting order the trader didn't intend to execute and no benefit from a one-sided order.
3. There was no public event or risk event in the window. Order-to-trade ratio is 40 against a typical 15.9, which fits continuous re-quoting. There were no repetitions of a spoofing cycle in the session.

**What would change my mind:** a large one-sided resting order, or bids left resting while the asks traded. A favourable price move that reverts after a cancel on a non-quote order would also change it.

I also looked at the two prior closures on this trader. The same market-making explanation holds on today's tape, but I used them as context only.
